rv.q: The result is—how you say?—exquisite.
"English" very rightfully won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama in 2023, and it's hands down a masterpiece of theater.
Absolutely nothing gets lost in the translation of Sanaz Toossi’s English as the Pulitzer Prize-winning play about a group of Iranians longing for the West finally makes its Broadway debut.
The exquisite Broadway production from director Knud Adams is the first must-see play of the season, and its lessons are likely to stick.

Now that production, with director Knud Adams and the whole of the original cast and design team, arrives on Broadway like a welcome guest, a hopeful presence in a moment that feels like a particularly dismal party.
Toossi, an Iranian American playwright, understands this intimately and delves into the complexities of forging identity across languages in her warm, perceptive new play.

A delicate, buoyant comedy about a small group of adults studying the language of the title, the play disarms and delights with its depiction of ordinary Iranian citizens seeking with determination to expand the horizons of their lives.
To speak in English in order to function in a new place, the play argues, forces non-native speakers to live forever in that gap.
English, Sanaz Toossi’s stunning Broadway debut, is a precise study of language’s significance.
The actual show, then, is a surprise: a gentle, subtle experience that calibrates our ears to shifts in pedagogy and understanding.
Book a ticket right now—an exquisitely written, beautifully acted and mounted one hour and forty-five minutes of theater awaits.
In any language, English is a triumph: Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer Prize-winning play is a compelling exploration of how language shapes who we are and how we navigate the world.
With empathy in short supply these days, English is a welcome reminder of what it feels like.
With its Broadway transfer, English seems to have found a universal language.
Toossi writes organically, and as directed by Knud Adams with little fanfare, the work is unflinchingly honest which is to say it resists any effort to pump up the drama.
Adams is to be commended for guiding this excellent cast in doing uniformly fine work.
Because the performances are so strong, the cast members are able to mine English for every nuance of humor and individuality that is available to them.
It just doesn’t feel as deep as it did in 2022.

It is my fervent hope that English sparks curiosity for some of the Americans in the audience regarding how it would feel to migrate to a new world and prepare yourself mentally and physically to assimilate.
English is an absorbing snapshot of people in transition, seeking reinvention and self-improvement while worrying if they will shed too much of what makes them themselves.
Overall, “English” is a heartfelt, honest, and witty play.

cn.t: Toossi's Pulitzer-winning drama about Iranians learning English earns widespread praise for its smart, sensitive exploration of language and identity. Critics laud the gentle, moving storytelling and strong performances, though some find it slow-moving.

vs.sum: Completed a major renovation in early 2026 with all seats replaced and legroom expanded, making it one of Broadway's most comfortable and modern houses. New restrooms significantly reduce intermission wait times.

acc.note: Elevators to all levels. 53 assistive listening devices. 11 wheelchair seats across Orchestra and Balcony.
